sections.markdown:
## C — Hill parking, freeways, lane changes and passing

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A01
Where parallel parking is allowed, park within 12 inches of the curb, or as near as possible to the outer edge of the shoulder, so traffic is not blocked or slowed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A01
Parked facing downhill beside a curb, turn the front wheels toward the curb and let the car roll gently until the front tire rests against it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A01
Parked facing uphill beside a curb, point the front wheels away from it and ease backward until the rear of the front tire is blocked by the curb. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A01
With no curb, turn the front wheels to the right whether facing uphill or downhill, so a rolling car would leave the highway instead of entering traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A01
Freeways are dangerous because of the high speeds involved, so stay aware of everything around you at all times. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A01
On an acceleration ramp, build up speed to match freeway traffic before you merge. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A01
To enter from a side entrance ramp, signal, look for a gap, speed up to the traffic speed and merge only when it is safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A01
Do not merge until the solid white line ends, avoid stopping in the acceleration lane unless truly necessary, and remember that freeway traffic has the right-of-way. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A01
On a metered entrance ramp, stop at the signal and enter the freeway only when released by a green light. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A01
Freeways are built to carry more traffic at higher speeds than ordinary streets or highways. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A01
Use the rightmost lane when you are going slower than normal traffic speed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A01
The leftmost passing lane is for passing, left turns, and times when heavy traffic leaves no room to merge into the other lanes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A01
Approaching a merge area, move over when it is safe to give entering vehicles room. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A01
On the freeway, watch traffic ahead, beside and behind you, stay aware of vehicles in your blind spots, and plan ahead with directional and guide signs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A01
On the freeway, signal at least 200 feet before a lane change, avoid changing lanes often, and never drive across, over or inside a median or island. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A02
To exit, use the deceleration lane: signal 200 feet before it begins, hold your speed until you are in it, then slow to the advised exit ramp speed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A02
When leaving a freeway, keep pace with traffic until the exit, do not exit at the last second, and do not exceed the posted ramp limit. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A02
A lane change includes moving between lanes, passing, merging from an entrance ramp and pulling onto the road from a curb or shoulder, and each requires checking ahead, beside and behind. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A02
A blind spot is an area slightly to the side and rear of your vehicle that neither the rearview nor side mirrors show. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A02
To change lanes, signal for at least 3 seconds or 200 feet, check ahead, check the mirrors, look over your shoulder at the blind spot, then move over when safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A02
Once centered in the new lane, glance at the mirror for traffic behind you, and switch the signal off no more than 3 seconds after the change is complete. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A02
Signs and markings show where passing is and is not allowed, and passing is normally done on the left. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A02
Passing on the right is allowed only on one-way streets and on roads with two or more lanes each way, and passing by driving off the pavement or on the shoulder is never allowed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A02
Before passing anyone, bicyclists included, judge from traffic ahead, beside and behind whether you have enough time and room to do it safely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A02
To pass, change lanes properly, speed up past the vehicle, and return to your lane once both of its headlights appear in your rearview mirror. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A02
When passing a bicyclist, keep at least three feet between the rider and the outermost part of your vehicle, including mirrors or a trailer. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A02
To pass a bicyclist you may briefly cross a solid yellow line when no traffic is oncoming and your view ahead is clear. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A02
Give bicyclists extra room on rural roads, in a large vehicle or in wind, because a wind blast can knock a rider over. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A02
Pass only one vehicle at a time rather than counting on passing several at once. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-F30 | anchor: A02
Never start a pass unless you can be back on the right side while still more than 200 feet from any oncoming vehicle, counting a bicyclist on the oncoming lane or shoulder. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-F31 | anchor: A02
Do not pass if you cannot get back to the right side before a solid yellow line begins. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]
